dirty_state_caveat: Shared worktree with five concurrent lanes. Social changed only app/api interaction routes and __tests__/social; it authored no migration.
summary: The shipped RLS posture leaves two interaction tables readable by any caller at the database layer: `post_likes` has SELECT policy "Anyone can view likes" USING (true) and `post_comments` has SELECT policy "Comments are viewable by everyone" USING (true). SOCIAL-007 closed the service-role read leak in app/api, but it cannot make the database itself refuse a cross-user interaction read: an authenticated or anonymous PostgREST caller can still select every row of those two tables for any post id. Social therefore made the application-layer post-visibility gate mandatory and fail-closed, but that is defense in depth only. Tightening the two SELECT policies is the durable fix and needs database ownership because it has client-side blast radius.

findings.current_policy: CREATE POLICY "Anyone can view likes" ON post_likes FOR SELECT USING (true)
findings.impact: Any caller can enumerate every liker of every post, including followers-only and private posts, straight through PostgREST.

findings.current_policy: CREATE POLICY "Comments are viewable by everyone" ON post_comments FOR SELECT USING (true)
findings.impact: Any caller can read every comment body on every post, including followers-only and private posts.

findings.current_policy: CREATE POLICY "Users can view their own shares" ON post_shares FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id)
findings.impact: Already correct. This is the reference shape the other two tables should converge on.

completed: Application-layer boundary is now mandatory and fail-closed: GET /api/notifications/social and GET /api/posts/[id]/poll/vote call resolvePostCommentAccess before any interaction read and return one indistinguishable 404.
app/api/notifications/social no longer holds a service-role read path at all; it reads through the caller-scoped client so post_shares RLS genuinely applies.
19 focused negative tests in __tests__/social/interaction-notification-isolation.test.ts and 10 in __tests__/social/poll-interaction-isolation.test.ts prove the app gate and the fail-closed behavior.
next_steps: Author one strictly additive, forward-only migration that replaces the two USING (true) SELECT policies on post_likes and post_comments with a policy set that requires an entitled viewer, and never apply it locally (CP-051) — author and hand the manifest to the operator.

Decide the entitlement predicate with the feed lane before writing the policy. A reusable SECURITY DEFINER helper that answers 'may auth.uid() read interactions for post <id>?' is preferable to duplicating the visibility CASE expression in two policies, because posts.visibility, posts.is_visible, posts.moderation_status, follows and account_follows must all agree with lib/feed/post-comment-access.ts.

Audit the client-side blast radius before the policy lands: components/artist/artist-home-feed.tsx:186 and components/profile/public-profile-view.tsx:284 read post_likes directly from the browser and currently rely on USING (true). If the new policy would break those surfaces, move them behind an authorized API first, in the owning lanes.

After the policy is applied on an approved target, rerun SIM-20260922-SOC-003 with sim-customer-01 (outsider) and sim-artist-01 (owner) against a direct PostgREST read, not just the app route, so the database boundary itself is proven.
